display.text:
# Run `make bootstrap` to set up your local environment.
# To build using go, use `make build`
# For a binary that's in parity with how our CI system builds,
# run `make goreleaser` to build using GoReleaser Pro.

# Variables:
# V=1 for verbose output.

# the name of the executable
BINNAME?=step

# the build output path
PREFIX?=bin

# the install path
DESTDIR?=/usr/local/bin

# GOOS_OVERRIDE="GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm GOARM=6" to change OS and arch
GOOS_OVERRIDE?=

# CGO_OVERRIDE="CGO_ENABLED=1" to enable CGO
CGO_OVERRIDE?=CGO_ENABLED=0

# which build id in .goreleaser.yml to build
GORELEASER_BUILD_ID?=default

# all go files
SRC=$(shell find . -type f -name '*.go' -or -name go.mod -or -name go.sum)

all: lint test build

ci: test build

.PHONY: all ci

#################################################
# Determine the type of `push` and `version`
#################################################

ifdef GITHUB_REF
VERSION ?= $(shell echo $(GITHUB_REF) | sed 's/^refs\/tags\///')
NOT_RC  := $(shell echo $(VERSION) | grep -v -e -rc)
	ifeq ($(NOT_RC),)
PUSHTYPE := release-candidate
	else
PUSHTYPE := release
	endif
else
VERSION ?= $(shell [ -d .git ] && git describe --tags --always --dirty="-dev")
# If we are not in an active git dir then try reading the version from .VERSION.
# .VERSION contains a slug populated by `git archive`.
VERSION := $(or $(VERSION),$(shell make/version.sh .VERSION))
PUSHTYPE := branch
endif

VERSION := $(shell echo $(VERSION) | sed 's/^v//')

ifdef V
$(info    GITHUB_REF is $(GITHUB_REF))
$(info    VERSION is $(VERSION))
$(info    PUSHTYPE is $(PUSHTYPE))
endif

DATE    := $(shell date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC')
ifdef DEBUG
	LDFLAGS := -ldflags='-X "main.Version=$(VERSION)" -X "main.BuildTime=$(DATE)"'
	GCFLAGS := -gcflags "all=-N -l"
else
	LDFLAGS := -ldflags='-w -X "main.Version=$(VERSION)" -X "main.BuildTime=$(DATE)"'
	GCFLAGS :=
endif

Q=$(if $V,,@)
OUTPUT_ROOT=output/

ifeq ($(OS),Windows_NT)
	HOSTOS=Windows
else
	HOSTOS=$(shell uname)
endif

HOSTARCH=$(shell go env GOHOSTARCH)
ifeq ($(HOSTARCH),amd64)
       HOSTARCH=x86_64
endif

GORELEASER_PRO_URL=https://github.com/goreleaser/goreleaser-pro/releases/latest/download/goreleaser-pro_$(HOSTOS)_$(HOSTARCH).tar.gz

# Determine the hooks to skip. When using GoReleaser OSS with a Pro config, specifying "after"
# to be skipped results in an error. When using GoReleaser Pro running the "goreleaser-local"
# target both "post-hooks" and "after" are required to skip the upload to GCP. The logic below 
# checks the GoReleaser binary to be Pro or not, and then sets the steps to skip accordingly. 
# It's possible this is a GoReleaser bug for the case where a Pro config is used with GoReleaser 
# OSS.
GORELEASER_OSS_SKIP=post-hooks
GORELEASER_PRO_SKIP=post-hooks,after
GORELEASER_SKIP=$(if $(filter true,$(shell goreleaser --version | grep -q goreleaser-pro && echo true || echo false)),$(GORELEASER_PRO_SKIP),$(GORELEASER_OSS_SKIP))

.PHONY: all

#########################################
# Bootstrapping
#########################################
TMPDIR := $(shell mktemp -d)
bootstra%: GOPATH=$(shell go env GOPATH)
bootstra%:
	$Q curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/golangci/golangci-lint/master/install.sh | sh -s -- -b $$(go env GOPATH)/bin latest
	$Q go install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest
	$Q go install gotest.tools/gotestsum@latest
	$Q go install golang.org/x/tools/cmd/goimports@latest
	@echo "Installing GoReleaser Pro into $(GOPATH)/bin"
	$Q curl -o $(TMPDIR)/goreleaser.tar.gz -L $(GORELEASER_PRO_URL)
	$Q ls $(TMPDIR)
	$Q tar xvzf $(TMPDIR)/goreleaser.tar.gz -C $(TMPDIR)
	$Q cp $(TMPDIR)/goreleaser $(GOPATH)/bin

.PHONY: bootstra%

#########################################
# Build
#########################################

build: $(PREFIX)/$(BINNAME)
	@echo "Build Complete!"

$(PREFIX)/$(BINNAME): $(SRC)
	$Q mkdir -p $(PREFIX)
	$Q $(GOOS_OVERRIDE) $(CGO_OVERRIDE) go build \
		-v \
	   	-o $(PREFIX)/$(BINNAME) \
		$(GCFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) \
	   	github.com/smallstep/cli/cmd/step

goreleaser:
	$Q mkdir -p $(PREFIX)
	$Q $(GOOS_OVERRIDE) $(CGO_OVERRIDE) DEBUG=$(DEBUG) goreleaser build \
		--id $(GORELEASER_BUILD_ID) \
	   	--snapshot \
		--single-target \
	   	--clean \
		--skip=$(GORELEASER_SKIP) \
		--output $(PREFIX)/$(BINNAME)

.PHONY: build goreleaser


#########################################
# Test
#########################################

test:
	$Q $(CGO_OVERRIDE) $(GOFLAGS) gotestsum -- -coverprofile=coverage.out -short -covermode=atomic ./...

race:
	$Q $(CGO_OVERRIDE) $(GOFLAGS) gotestsum -- -race ./...

.PHONY: test race

#########################################
# Linting
#########################################

fmt:
	$Q goimports -local github.com/golangci/golangci-lint -l -w $(SRC)

lint: golint govulncheck

golint: SHELL:=/bin/bash
golint:
	$Q LOG_LEVEL=error golangci-lint run --config <(curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallstep/workflows/master/.golangci.yml) --timeout=30m

govulncheck:
	$Q govulncheck ./...

.PHONY: fmt lint golint govulncheck

#########################################
# Install
#########################################

install: $(PREFIX)/$(BINNAME)
	$Q mkdir -p $(DESTDIR)/
	$Q install $(PREFIX)/$(BINNAME) $(DESTDIR)/$(BINNAME)

uninstall:
	$Q rm -f $(DESTDIR)/$(BINNAME)

.PHONY: install uninstall

#########################################
# Clean
#########################################

clean:
	$Q rm -f $(PREFIX)/$(BINNAME)
	$Q rm -rf dist

.PHONY: clean

#################################################
# Build statically compiled step binary for various operating systems
#################################################

BINARY_OUTPUT=$(OUTPUT_ROOT)binary/

define BUNDLE_MAKE
	# $(1) -- Go Operating System (e.g. linux, darwin, windows, etc.)
	# $(2) -- Go Architecture (e.g. amd64, arm, arm64, etc.)
	# $(3) -- Go ARM architectural family (e.g. 7, 8, etc.)
	# $(4) -- Parent directory for executables generated by 'make'.
	$Q GOOS_OVERRIDE='GOOS=$(1) GOARCH=$(2) GOARM=$(3)' PREFIX=$(4) make $(4)/$(BINNAME)
endef

binary-linux-amd64:
	$(call BUNDLE_MAKE,linux,amd64,,$(BINARY_OUTPUT)linux-amd64)

binary-linux-arm64:
	$(call BUNDLE_MAKE,linux,arm64,,$(BINARY_OUTPUT)linux-arm64)

binary-linux-armv7:
	$(call BUNDLE_MAKE,linux,arm,7,$(BINARY_OUTPUT)linux-armv7)

binary-linux-mips:
	$(call BUNDLE_MAKE,linux,mips,,$(BINARY_OUTPUT)linux-mips)

binary-darwin-amd64:
	$(call BUNDLE_MAKE,darwin,amd64,,$(BINARY_OUTPUT)darwin-amd64)

binary-darwin-arm64:
	$(call BUNDLE_MAKE,darwin,arm64,,$(BINARY_OUTPUT)darwin-arm64)

binary-windows-amd64:
	$(call BUNDLE_MAKE,windows,amd64,,$(BINARY_OUTPUT)windows-amd64)

.PHONY: binary-linux-amd64 binary-linux-arm64 binary-linux-armv7 binary-linux-mips binary-darwin-amd64 binary-darwin-arm64 binary-windows-amd64

---

# Step CLI Command Architecture Report

## 1. Entrypoint dispatch flow

### `cmd/step/main.go` (29 lines, intentionally trivial)

- `main()` at `cmd/step/main.go:27-29` does nothing but call `cmd.Run()` from `github.com/smallstep/cli/internal/cmd`.
- `init()` at `cmd/step/main.go:21-25` sets build metadata before anything runs:
  - `step.Set("Smallstep CLI", Version, BuildTime)` — `Version`/`BuildTime` are LDFLAG-injected vars (lines 10–16).
  - `ca.UserAgent = step.Version()` — user-agent for step-ca API clients.
  - `cmd.SetName(AppName)` — allows the binary name to differ from `step` (e.g., `step-beta`).

### `internal/cmd/root.go` — the real dispatcher

- **`Run()`** (`internal/cmd/root.go:46-48`): `os.Exit(run())`.
- **`run()`** (`internal/cmd/root.go:50-85`):
  1. `defer panicHandler()` (line 51).
  2. `step.Init()` initializes the `$STEPPATH` environment (lines 54–57); failure prints to stderr and returns exit code 1.
  3. Builds the app with `newApp(os.Stdout, os.Stderr)` (line 60) and runs `app.Run(os.Args)`.
  4. **Error handling** (lines 62–82): if the returned error implements `interface { Message() string }` (the `errs.Error` type from cli-utils), it prints `err.Message()` to stderr; with `STEPDEBUG=1` it prints the full `%+v` stack plus the message. Otherwise it prints `err` (or `%+v` under `STEPDEBUG=1`). Returns 1 on any error, 0 on success.
- **`newApp()`** (`internal/cmd/root.go:95-154`):
  - Injects file-writing and password-prompt callbacks into `go.step.sm/crypto` so `pemutil.WriteFile`, `pemutil.PromptPassword`, and `jose.PromptPassword` use CLI-consistent implementations (`fileutil.WriteFile`, `ui.PromptPassword`) — lines 97–103.
  - Overrides urfave/cli globals (lines 106–114): `cli.VersionPrinter` → `version.Command`; help/command templates from `usage` package; custom `HelpPrinter`, `FlagNamePrefixer`, and `FlagStringer` (`stringifyFlag`, lines 182–194, extracts `<...>` placeholders from flag usage strings).
  - `app.Commands = command.Retrieve()` (line 122) — pulls every command registered by package `init()` functions. The blank imports at lines 25–44 are what wire the tree: CAS backends (`cloudcas`, `softcas`, `stepcas`) plus all 14 command packages.
  - App flags: built-in `--help` plus a global `--config` flag (lines 128–131); `EnableBashCompletion = true`.
  - **Fallback `app.Action`** (lines 134–147) — special handling for unknown first arguments:
    - `plugin.LookPath(name)` succeeds → run it as a plugin (`plugin.Run`); this is the `step <plugin-name>` exec path (e.g., `step-kms-plugin`).
    - `plugin.GetURL(name)` returns a known download URL → error "The plugin %q was not found on this system. Download it from %s".
    - Otherwise → `cli.ShowCommandHelp(ctx, name)`; with no args → `cli.ShowAppHelp`.
- **`panicHandler()`** (`internal/cmd/root.go:156-170`): recovers panics; with `STEPDEBUG=1` it re-panics after printing version/date; otherwise prints a friendly "Something unexpected happened" message with the `STEPDEBUG=1` repro command and exits with code **2**.

## 2. Command registration model

There is no `command/command.go` in this repo — registration lives in the external module `github.com/smallstep/cli-utils v0.12.2` (declared at `go.mod:21`). Its `command` package (verified from upstream source) is a global registry:

- `var cmds []cli.Command`, seeded in `init()` with `usage.HelpCommand()`.
- `Register(c cli.Command)` — appends the command and propagates env-var names via `step.SetEnvVar`.
- `Retrieve() []cli.Command` — returns the registry (called by `newApp`).
- `ActionFunc(fn cli.ActionFunc) cli.ActionFunc` — wraps an action to stash the current `*cli.Context` in a package var, powering `command.IsForce()`. Most commands wrap their action in this.

Per `command/README.md`, each command package registers itself in `init()`; top-level packages are then blank-imported in `internal/cmd/root.go` so their `init()` runs. The repo's own `internal/command` package (see §5) provides a separate, orthogonal helper for context injection.

## 3. Full command tree (names only)

Sources: group `init()`/`Command()` files per package. Depth beyond 3 shown where verified.

- **api** (hidden) — `command/api/api.go`
  - token — `command/api/token/token.go`: create
- **base64** (leaf action) — `command/base64/base64.go`
- **beta** — `command/beta/beta.go`
  - ca (via `ca.BetaCommand()`, `command/ca/ca.go:159`): acme → eab (list, add, remove)
- **ca** — `command/ca/ca.go`
  - health, init, bootstrap, token, certificate, rekey, renew, revoke
  - provisioner (`command/ca/provisioner/provisioner.go`): list, jwe-key, add, update, remove, webhook (add, update, remove)
  - sign, root, roots, federation
  - acme (`command/ca/acme/acme.go`): eab (list, add, remove)

## 4. Implementation pattern for a single command

Reference: `command/certificate/create.go` (934 lines) — the canonical example.

**a. Command definition as a package-private constructor returning `cli.Command`:**
- `createCommand()` at `command/certificate/create.go:41-493` returns a `cli.Command` with `Name: "create"`, `Action: command.ActionFunc(createAction)` (line 44), `Usage`, a long `UsageText` with bold `**flags**` markers, a long markdown-ish `Description` with `## POSITIONAL ARGUMENTS`, `## EXIT CODES`, `## TEMPLATES`, `## EXAMPLES` sections (single quotes `'''` are converted to backticks by the usage package's help printer).
- **Flags** (lines 391–491): mix of shared constructors from `github.com/smallstep/cli/flags` (`flags.KTY`, `flags.Size`, `flags.Curve`, `flags.Template`, `flags.KMSUri`, `flags.Force`, `flags.Subtle`, `flags.InsecureHidden`) and inline `cli.StringFlag`/`cli.BoolFlag`/`cli.StringSliceFlag` definitions with long, structured usage strings (the `: <value>` indented style documents enumerations).

**b. The action function** — `createAction(ctx *cli.Context) error` at `command/certificate/create.go:495-771`. The pattern is strictly sequential:
1. **Argument validation first** via the `errs` package: `errs.MinMaxNumberOfArguments` (line 500), `errs.EqualArguments` (line 514). Every validation failure returns an `errs.*` error immediately (fail-fast guard clauses).
2. **Flag parsing**: read flags with `ctx.String(...)`/`ctx.Bool(...)`/`ctx.IsSet(...)` into locals (lines 504–536); cross-flag validation with `errs.RequiredWithFlag`, `errs.IncompatibleFlagWithFlag`, `errs.InvalidFlagValue` (lines 506–543, 574–594).
3. **Helpers to decompose logic**: `parseOrCreateKey` (lines 773–836) handles KMS/file key loading via `internal/cryptoutil` (`cryptoutil.CreateSigner`, `cryptoutil.PublicKey`, `cryptoutil.IsX509Signer`); `parseSigner` (lines 841–909) resolves the issuing CA; `savePrivateKey` (lines 912–934) handles encryption/password prompting.
4. **Business logic** via `go.step.sm/crypto` libraries: `x509util.CreateTemplateData` + `x509util.NewCertificate(..., WithTemplate(...))` (lines 692–713), `x509util.CreateCertificate` (line 735), `pemutil.Serialize` (line 741).
5. **Output** through the `ui` package, which renders go-template strings with color filters: `ui.Printf("Your certificate has been saved in %s.\n", crtFile)` at lines 634–637 and 765–768. (Other commands use `ui.PrintSelected`, `ui.Select`, `ui.PromptPassword` with options like `ui.WithValidateNotEmpty()` — see line 926.)
6. **Return `nil` on success**; any error propagates up to `run()` in `internal/cmd/root.go`, where `errs.Error`'s `Message()` gets printed (and `STEPDEBUG=1` reveals stacks).

The same shape appears in smaller leaf commands: `command/base64/base64.go:85-117` (`base64Action`), `command/fileserver/fileserver.go:94-185`, `command/crypto/kdf/kdf.go:160-203` (`hashAction`), and `command/completion/completion.go:100-123` (`Completion`).

**c. Group registration pattern** — e.g. `command/certificate/certificate.go:10-102`: an `init()` builds a parent `cli.Command` whose `Subcommands` slice calls each `xxxCommand()` constructor, then calls `command.Register(cmd)`. Files per command; one group file per package. Some groups take parameters (`policy.Command()` passes a `context.Context` down through `command/ca/policy/policy.go:14-27`; `internal/command.InjectContext` is used to carry it into actions).

## 5. `internal/command` — helper abstractions

`internal/command/inject.go` (56 lines) provides Go-`context` bridging for commands that need cancellation/values beyond `*cli.Context`:

- `InjectContext(injectedCtx context.Context, fn func(context.Context) error, middleware ...func(context.Context) (context.Context, error)) cli.ActionFunc` (lines 14–23): returns a `cli.ActionFunc` that installs the injected context as the first middleware, applies optional middleware chain, stores the `*cli.Context` inside the context, and calls `fn(ctx)`.
- `withCLIContext` / `CLIContextFromContext` (lines 28–36): typed key to retrieve the `*cli.Context` from a `context.Context` (panics if absent).
- `wrap` (lines 40–56): the middleware executor.

Used heavily by the `ca policy` subtree (`command/ca/policy/...` takes a `ctx context.Context` through every `Command(ctx)` constructor).

Other notable helper packages referenced by commands:
- `flags` (`/tmp/openwiki-bench-Wlyt8n/flags/flags.go`): shared flag constructors (`KTY`, `Curve`, `Size`, `Force`, `Subtle`, `HiddenNoContext`, `InsecureHidden`, `Template*`) plus `ParseTimeOrDuration`, `GetTemplateData`, `ParseTemplateData`.
- `errs` (external, cli-utils): typed errors and validators (`NumberOfArguments`, `InvalidFlagValue`, `RequiredWithFlag`, `IncompatibleFlagWithFlag`, `FileError`, `EqualArguments`, ...).
- `usage` (external, cli-utils): templates/printers wired in `newApp`.
- `ui` (external, cli-utils): templated terminal output, prompts, selects.
- `utils` (`/tmp/openwiki-bench-Wlyt8n/utils/`): `ReadInput`, `ReadString`, `ReadPasswordFromFile`, `GetKeyDetailsFromCLI`; `utils/cautils` holds the CA interaction flows (`certificate_flow.go`, `token_flow.go`, `acme_flow.go`, `offline.go`, `client.go`).
- `internal/plugin` + `exec/` (`exec/exec.go`): plugin discovery/execution and `OpenInBrowser` (used by oauth).
- `internal/cryptoutil`, `internal/kdf`, `internal/sshutil`, `internal/crlutil`, `internal/cast`, `internal/sliceutil`: domain helpers.

## 6. `command/README.md` conventions

- Hierarchy level = its own package where possible (`version`, `help` live in subpackages of `command`); shared non-business-logic packages go at repo top level (`flags`, `errs`).
- Register in `init()` via `command.Register(cmd)`; blank-import top-level command packages from `cmd/step/main.go` so init runs (note: in the current code those blank imports actually live in `internal/cmd/root.go:30-44` — the README predates the `internal/cmd` refactor).
- Prefer reusing `flags` package flags before defining new ones; add new prompts to `prompts`; command-specific errors stay in the command package, general ones in `errs`; the `usage.Argument` struct documents positional args.
- Hide commands (deprecated/unready) by setting `Hidden: true` on `cli.Command` — as done for `api` (`command/api/api.go:13`), `fileserver` (`command/fileserver/fileserver.go:30`), and the oauth `implicit`/`browser` flags.

## Notable takeaways

1. **Two `command` packages**: `github.com/smallstep/cli-utils/command` (global registry: `Register`/`Retrieve`/`ActionFunc`/`IsForce`) vs. `github.com/smallstep/cli/internal/command` (context injection middleware). Don't confuse them.
2. **Registration is entirely side-effect driven** — the command tree is assembled by blank imports in `internal/cmd/root.go`, not by a literal list in main.
3. **Plugin exec escape hatch**: unknown commands fall through to plugin lookup (binary on PATH or a known download URL) in the fallback `app.Action` (`internal/cmd/root.go:134-147`).
4. **Uniform error contract**: commands return errors; `errs.Error` (with `Message()`) controls user-facing text; `STEPDEBUG=1` toggles verbose `%+v` output; panics exit 2 with a support message.
5. **Consistent command anatomy**: `xxxCommand() cli.Command` constructor + `command.ActionFunc(xxxAction)` + guard-clause flag/arg validation with `errs` helpers + `ui`-based output + `go.step.sm/crypto` for all crypto work.
</task_result>
</task>

## 9. Renewal: `step ca renew`

File: `/tmp/openwiki-bench-Wlyt8n/command/ca/renew.go`

- Command def & flags (renew.go:43-231): `<crt-file> <key-file>`, **`--mtls`** (BoolT, default true; `--mtls=false` forces token flow, 166-170), `--ca-config`, **`--force`**, `--offline`, `--password-file`, `--kms`, `--out`, **`--expires-in`**, `--pid`/`--pid-file`, `--signal` (default SIGHUP), `--exec`, **`--daemon`**, **`--renew-period`**, `--ca-url`, `--root`, `--context`.

  - `--out` defaults to overwrite `<crt-file>` (247-250); root defaults to `pki.GetRootCAPath()` (252-255); `--expires-in` and `--renew-period` are mutually exclusive, `--renew-period` requires `--daemon` (262-278); `--pid`/`--pid-file` mutual exclusion + parsing (280-301).

[Y/n]" prompt; `--force` skips it).

<task id="ses_faabe2f6bffeYLvjvLC9nKI8Q8" state="completed">
<task_result>
# Research Report: smallstep `step` CLI — crypto toolkit, OAuth, SSH, and supporting subsystems

Repo: `/tmp/openwiki-bench-Wlyt8n` (module `github.com/smallstep/cli`, Go 1.25.8, `go.mod:1-3`)

Entry point: `cmd/step/main.go:27-29` → `internal/cmd/root.go:run()`. All command groups self-register via `command.Register` in `init()` and are blank-imported at `internal/cmd/root.go:31-43`. Notably `root.go:97-103` overrides `pemutil.PromptPassword` and `jose.PromptPassword` globals so `go.step.sm/crypto` prompts route through the CLI's `ui`.

Key external dependencies (from `go.mod`):
- `github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v3 v3.0.5` (go.mod:9) — underlying JOSE implementation.
- `go.step.sm/crypto v0.89.0` (go.mod:30) — `jose` wrapper (options, ReadKey/ReadKeySet, Claims, Signer/Encrypter, ValidateJWK), `pemutil`, `keyutil`, `kms`, `x509util`, `randutil`.
- `github.com/smallstep/certificates v0.30.2` (go.mod:19) — CA API client (`ca`, `api`, `pki`, `provisioner`, `templates`, `ca/identity`).
- `github.com/smallstep/cli-utils v0.12.2` (go.mod:21) — command framework, `ui`, `errs`, `fileutil`, `step` (contexts/defaults).
- `github.com/smallstep/truststore v0.13.0` (go.mod:24), `smallstep/certinfo` (go.mod:20), `urfave/cli v1.22.17` (go.mod:28), `golang.org/x/crypto` (go.mod:31), `github.com/google/uuid` (go.mod:12).

---

## 1. command/crypto — the JOSE toolkit

**Registration & philosophy** — `command/crypto/crypto.go:22-179`: `step crypto` registers `change-pass`, `create-key-pair`, `jwk`, `jwt`, `jwe`, `jws`, `jose`, `hash`, `kdf`, `key`, `nacl`, `otp`, `rand`, `winpe` (crypto.go:160-175). Misuse prevention: subtle/insecure primitives require `--subtle`/`--insecure` flags (crypto.go:32-37); documented minimums: 256-bit symmetric, 2048-bit RSA (crypto.go:51-61); P-256 default EC curve (crypto.go:113-115).

**Library layering (important invariant):** the CLI never imports go-jose directly — everything goes through `go.step.sm/crypto/jose`, which adds option builders (`jose.WithUse`, `WithAlg`, `WithKid`, `WithSubtle`, `WithNoDefaults`, `WithPasswordFile`, `WithPasswordPrompter`), `jose.ReadKey`/`ReadKeySet`, `jose.Decrypt`, `jose.ValidateJWK`, `jose.ValidateX5C/X5T`, `jose.Claims`. Verified none of these are defined in this repo (only `token`-package options are local, e.g. `token/options.go:220`).

**Subcommands:**
- `jose format` (`command/crypto/jose/jose.go:32-99`): stdin → strip whitespace (jose.go:101-106) → try `ParseEncrypted` then `ParseJWS` (jose.go:78-86) → swap compact↔JSON serialization via the `serializer` interface (jose.go:27-30).
- `jws sign/verify/inspect` (`command/crypto/jws/sign.go`, `verify.go`, `inspect.go`): same skeleton as JWT, plus `--typ/--cty/--jku/--jwk` headers (sign.go:294-319).
- `key` subpackage: `fingerprint/format/inspect/public/sign/verify` (PEM-level operations).
- Also `nacl`, `otp`, `rand`, `hash`, `kdf`, `winpe` groups.

**Password handling (cross-cutting):**
- `--password-file` → `jose.WithPasswordFile(...)`: jwt sign `command/crypto/jwt/sign.go:303-305`, jwt verify `verify.go:179-181`, jws sign `sign.go:250-252`, provisioner keys `utils/cautils/token_generator.go:347-358`.
- Interactive prompts: `ui.PromptPassword` directly (jwe decrypt `decrypt.go:123-126`) or via `jose.WithPasswordPrompter` callbacks (jwk keyset `keyset.go:135-138`, public `public.go:37-41`, thumbprint `thumbprint.go:40-44`, provisioner key `token_generator.go:406-410`).
- `utils.ReadPasswordFromFile`/`ReadStringPasswordFromFile` right-trim file contents (`utils/read.go:53-72`).
- `change-pass` re-encrypts PEM keys via pemutil or JWKs via `jose.Encrypt` (`command/crypto/change-pass.go:113-178`).

**JWK group** (`command/crypto/jwk/jwk.go:88-94`):
- `create` (`create.go:390-600`): private JWK encryption ON by default; `--no-password` requires `--insecure` (create.go:396-408). kty validation: EC forbids `--size` (create.go:434-437); RSA forbids `--crv`, enforces `keyutil.MinRSAKeyBytes*8` minimum unless `--insecure` (create.go:443-451); oct forbids `--crv`, min 16 bytes (create.go:461-468). Generation via `jose.GenerateJWK` / `GenerateJWKFromPEM` (create.go:474-480). Default `kid` = SHA-256 thumbprint, base64url — skipped for oct keys because hashing a symmetric key can leak info (create.go:486-496). Private JWK serialized as a **JWE** with `PBES2_HS256_A128KW`, `PBES2Count: 600000` iterations (OWASP Dec-2022), 16-byte salt, content type `jwk+json` (constants create.go:26-35; encrypt block create.go:531-586); fallback if PBKDF2 unsupported: random 32-char `A128KW` password printed to user (create.go:553-561). Files 0600 (create.go:519, 593).
- `keyset add/remove/list/find` (`keyset.go`): all go through `rwLockKeySet` (keyset.go:228-309) — file `flock`ed via `sysutils.FileLock` (keyset.go:240-251), rewritten with truncate+`WriteAt` (keyset.go:283-293). `add` reads a possibly-JWE-encrypted JWK from stdin (keyset.go:129-145); `remove` filters by kid (keyset.go:173-181). Invariant: duplicate kids allowed per RFC7517 (comment keyset.go:153-156).
- `public` (`public.go:29-64`): decrypt → `Public()`; oct keys copied as-is because go-jose returns an empty public key for symmetric (public.go:50-55).
- `thumbprint` (`thumbprint.go:32-57`): SHA-256 thumbprint, base64url.

---

## 2. JWT and JWE flows: key loading, verification, kid lookup

### `step crypto jwt sign` (`command/crypto/jwt/sign.go:216-464`)
1. Payload from stdin/file/`-` (sign.go:220-235; `readPayload` sign.go:466-501 handles empty-stdin → `{}`, CI pipe EOF → valid empty JSON at 490-494).
2. Key sources, mutually exclusive (sign.go:237-287): `--key` (JWK or PEM, possibly encrypted), `--jwks` **requiring** `--kid` (sign.go:284-286), or `--x5c-cert`+`--x5c-key` / `--x5t-cert`+`--x5t-key`. Read via `jose.ReadKey`/`jose.ReadKeySet` with `WithUse("sig")`, `WithAlg`, `WithKid`, `WithSubtle`, `WithPasswordFile` options (sign.go:292-323).
3. Invariants: public keys cannot sign (sign.go:326-328); JWK `use` must be `sig`/empty (sign.go:331-333); `jose.ValidateJWK` (sign.go:342); alg must be resolvable — from `--alg`, the JWK, or guessed — else error (sign.go:339-341); `--exp` in future unless `--subtle` (sign.go:347-349); iss/aud/sub/exp required unless `--subtle` (sign.go:383-396); random 256-bit `jti` auto-generated (sign.go:351-356).
4. Signing: `jose.NewSigner` with `typ=JWT`, `kid` header unless hidden `--no-kid` (sign.go:399-403), extra string `--header k=v` (sign.go:406-412), `x5c`/`x5cInsecure` (sign.go:414-428) or `x5t` (sign.go:430-440). Single-value `aud` forced to string via claim overwrite (sign.go:450-455). Compact output (sign.go:457-462).

### `step crypto jwt verify` (`command/crypto/jwt/verify.go:118-250`)
1. `jose.ParseSigned` on stdin (verify.go:119-127).
2. **kid lookup in keyset:** `--key` xor `--jwks`; with `--jwks` the kid is either the `--kid` flag or, if absent, taken from the token's own `kid` header (verify.go:139-144), then passed as `jose.WithKid(kid)` so the matching member of the JWK Set is selected by `go.step.sm/crypto/jose` `ReadKeySet` (verify.go:183-195).
3. Anti-downgrade: when not `--insecure`, `jose.WithNoDefaults(true)` is added so no default algorithm is guessed (verify.go:176-178); `iss`/`aud` required unless `--subtle` (verify.go:150-157); hidden `--no-exp-check` requires `--insecure` (verify.go:160-162).
4. Structural rejections: multiple signatures (verify.go:209-211), `crit` header (verify.go:212-214), `--alg` vs header mismatch (verify.go:215-217).
5. Signature verification: `tok.Claims(publicKey(jwk), &claims)`; `publicKey` returns `jwk.Key` for symmetric, `jwk.Public().Key` otherwise (verify.go:111-116, 219-225). `jose.ErrCryptoFailure` → "validation failed: invalid signature" (verify.go:221-223).
6. **Custom claim validation** (`validateClaimsWithLeeway`, verify.go:254-297): re-implements go-jose `ValidateWithLeeway` but aggregates all errors into one message ("validation failed: ...") — checks iss/sub/jti/aud/nbf/exp; exp check skippable via `no-exp-check` (verify.go:286-290).

### `step crypto jwe encrypt` (`command/crypto/jwe/encrypt.go:158-293`)
- Content enc default `A256GCM` (encrypt.go:97; mapping 295-314); key alg mapping `getRecipientAlg` (encrypt.go:316-357): RSA1_5/RSA-OAEP(-256), A{128,192,256}KW, `dir`, ECDH-ES(+KW), GCMKW, PBES2-*
- **PBES2 mode**: no key file; password prompted (encrypt.go:227) and used as the raw recipient key (encrypt.go:236-241); mutually exclusive with `--key`/`--jwks` (encrypt.go:192-203).
- Public-key mode: `jwk.Public()` (encrypt.go:244-245), `use=sig` rejected (encrypt.go:247-249), `jose.ValidateJWK`, `jose.NewEncrypter(enc, recipient, opts)` → `FullSerialize()` (encrypt.go:281-291).

### `step crypto jwe decrypt` (`command/crypto/jwe/decrypt.go:59-163`)
- `jose.ParseEncrypted` (decrypt.go:74); alg read from JWE header to detect PBES2 (decrypt.go:79-85). PBES2 → password prompt (optionally prefilled from `--password-file`, decrypt.go:115-126); otherwise private key required — public key rejected (decrypt.go:139-141), `use=sig` rejected (decrypt.go:143-145) — then `obj.Decrypt(jwk.Key)` (decrypt.go:155-160).

**Invariants across JOSE commands:** `use` enforcement is bidirectional — enc keys can't sign, sig keys can't encrypt; private files 0600; JWK Sets are flock-protected; `--subtle`/`--insecure` gates everywhere.

---

## 3. command/oauth/cmd.go — OAuth 2.0 / OIDC

Registered as top-level `step oauth` (`command/oauth/cmd.go:79-307`).

**Providers** (`knownProviders`, cmd.go:573-586): hardcoded endpoints for **google** and **github** (authorization, device-authorization, token, userinfo). Any other `--provider` value must be an `https://` OIDC discovery URL — `disco()` fetches `/.well-known/openid-configuration` and extracts `authorization_endpoint`, `device_authorization_endpoint`, `token_endpoint` (cmd.go:684-709). Baked-in Google "installed app" client IDs/secrets: default client cmd.go:49-51, device-flow client cmd.go:54-56 (with rationale comments cmd.go:35-46).

**Flow selection** (cmd.go:495-509): service-account (`--account`, two-legged) → `DoTwoLeggedAuthorization`/`DoJWTAuthorization`; `--console`/`--console-flow device` → `DoDeviceAuthorization`; `--console-flow oob` → `DoManualAuthorization`; **default → `DoLoopbackAuthorization`**.

**Loopback authorization-code flow with browser + local server** (`DoLoopbackAuthorization`, cmd.go:768-814):
- Starts an HTTP server: `NewServer` (cmd.go:729-763) uses `httptest.NewServer(o)` — i.e. **random port on 127.0.0.1** — unless `--listen` is given (e.g. `:10000` or `0.0.0.0:10000` with `--listen-url` for the redirect URI); `--listen-url` path overrides `CallbackPath` (cmd.go:339-347).
- Builds the auth URL in `Auth()` (cmd.go:1198-1231): `response_type=code`, **PKCE S256** (`code_challenge_method=S256`, SHA-256 of a random 64-char challenge, cmd.go:1211-1213), `state` (random 32-char, cmd.go:589), `nonce` (256-bit, cmd.go:599), `scope` (default `"openid email"`, cmd.go:463), `prompt`, `login_hint` (`--email`), and extra `--auth-param`s.
- Opens the browser via `exec.OpenInBrowser(authURL, o.browser)` at cmd.go:790, unless `STEP_OPEN_BROWSER=0` (cmd.go:787-788), in which case the URL is printed. On failure, prints the URL (cmd.go:791-802).
- Waits on channels with a **2-minute timeout** (cmd.go:806-813).
- `ServeHTTP` (cmd.go:1092-1150) is the handler: serves only `CallbackPath` (default `/`), passes `OPTIONS` through (cmd.go:1098-1102), rejects `error` query param (cmd.go:1105-1109), validates `code`+`state` against the generated state (cmd.go:1116-1132), exchanges the code (cmd.go:1134), then 302-redirects to `--redirect-url` or serves the SVG "success" page (cmd.go:1144-1148), and ships the token over `tokCh`. Errors are reported via `badRequest` → `errCh` (cmd.go:1292-1324).
- `Exchange` (cmd.go:1234-1255): POST form `grant_type=authorization_code` + `code_verifier` (PKCE) + client creds; `postForm` (cmd.go:714-726) sets `Accept: application/json` (GitHub requirement) and `req.Close = true`.
- Hidden **implicit flow** (`--implicit` requires `--insecure` + `--client-id`, cmd.go:390-396): `implicitHandler` (cmd.go:1152-1195) serves a JS page that copies the URL hash fragment back to the server as query params (`urlhash=true`).

**Device Authorization Grant** (`DoDeviceAuthorization`, cmd.go:863-952; RFC 8628): POST to device endpoint; prefers `verification_uri_complete` (no user code needed) and tolerates Google's spec-violating `verification_url` (cmd.go:896-908); polls the token endpoint every `interval` seconds (default 5, cmd.go:58) until `expires_in` (cap default 5 min, cmd.go:59); `errHTTPToken` (4xx) keeps polling (cmd.go:940-947).

**OOB flow** (`DoManualAuthorization`, cmd.go:819-846): `redirect_uri = urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob` (cmd.go:62), user pastes the verification code.

**Service accounts** (`--account`): `installed`-type or `service_account` JSON (cmd.go:433-461). `DoTwoLeggedAuthorization` (cmd.go:983-1042) signs an RS256 JWT assertion (aud = token endpoint, `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer`, cmd.go:65). `DoJWTAuthorization --jwt` (cmd.go:1046-1088) returns a self-signed JWT without any network call.

**Token output** (cmd.go:515-535): `--header` → `Authorization: Bearer <tok>`; `--bare` → token only (`--oidc` selects ID token); default → pretty-printed full token JSON (`token` struct cmd.go:68-77 with access/id/**refresh** tokens, expiry, error fields). **Refresh tokens are only carried/parsed — no refresh grant is implemented** (RefreshToken appears only at cmd.go:71 and 1176).

**`exec.OpenInBrowser`** (`exec/exec.go:102-127`): darwin `open [-a <browser>]`; linux: WSL → `rundll32.exe url.dll,FileProtocolHandler`, else `xdg-open`; android `xdg-open`; windows `rundll32`; other platforms error. (WSL detection: reads `/proc/sys/kernel/osrelease`, exec.go:31-37.)

**Reuse by the CA flow:** `generateOIDCToken` (`utils/cautils/token_generator.go:144-169`) shells out to `step oauth --oidc --bare --provider <config-endpoint> --client-id ... [--console] [--listen <addr>]` via `exec.Step` (exec/exec.go:130-146) — the OIDC provisioner's `ListenAddress` is honored unless `STEP_LISTEN` is set (token_generator.go:161-163).

---

## 4. command/ssh

**Subcommands** (`command/ssh/ssh.go:84-100`): `certificate`, `check-host`, `config`, `fingerprint`, `hosts`, `inspect`, `list`, `login`, `logout`, `needs-renewal`, `proxycommand` (a legacy `proxyCommand()` is commented out at ssh.go:95), `rekey`, `renew`, `revoke`. Shared flags at ssh.go:106-162. Helpers: `loginOnUnauthorized` (ssh.go:164-252) — a `ca.WithRetryFunc` that, on 401 with `RequireClientAuthentication`, generates an OIDC identity token, creates an x509 identity CSR via `ca.CreateIdentityRequest`, calls `SSHSign` with `IdentityCSR`, writes the default identity (`ca.WriteDefaultIdentity`), and best-effort adds the cert to the agent; `createPrincipalsFromSubject` (ssh.go:298-311).

### `step ssh certificate` (`command/ssh/certificate.go:221-549`)
1. Args `<key-id> <key-file>`; outputs `<key>`, `<key>.pub`, `<key>-cert.pub` (certificate.go:229-232).
2. Cert/token type: host → `provisioner.SSHHostCert` + `cautils.SSHHostSignType`, user → `SSHUserCert` + `SSHUserSignType` (certificate.go:295-301). Default principals from subject (certificate.go:304-310).
3. Key: `--sign` parses an existing authorized key (certificate.go:318-334) else `keyutil.GenerateKeyPair(kty, curve, size)` (certificate.go:337).
4. **Token acquisition**: `flow := cautils.NewCertificateFlow(ctx)` (certificate.go:348); unless `--token`, `flow.GenerateSSHToken(ctx, subject, tokType, principals, validAfter, validBefore)` (certificate.go:352-356). `CertificateFlow.GenerateSSHToken` (`utils/cautils/certificate_flow.go:209-231`): offline mode → `OfflineCA.GenerateToken`; online → requires `--ca-url` and root (default `$STEPPATH/...root_ca` via `pki.GetRootCAPath()`) and calls `NewTokenFlow`.
5. `NewTokenFlow` (`utils/cautils/token_flow.go:101-183`): audience derived from ca-url + type-specific path — `/1.0/ssh/sign` for both SSH user/host types (token_flow.go:59-60); fetches provisioners via `pki.GetProvisioners(caURL, root)`; interactive `provisionerPrompt` (token_flow.go:291-408, filters by x5c/sshpop/nebula/k8s flags, `--kid`, `--provisioner`; auto-selects when single); dispatches per provisioner type (token_flow.go:154-182): JWK → `generateJWKToken`; OIDC → `generateOIDCToken` (spawns `step oauth`, see §3); X5C → `generateX5CToken` (KMS-aware signer, token_generator.go:195-273); Nebula (275-311); SSHPOP (313-345); K8sSA reads the service-account token file (183-193); GCP/AWS/Azure → `GetIdentityToken` (167-175).
6. `generateJWKToken` (`token_generator.go:441-469`) + `loadJWK` (380-439): with `--key` loads from file or **KMS** via `cryptoutil.LoadJSONWebKey(ctx.String("kms"), keyFile, ...)` (token_generator.go:422); otherwise fetches the provisioner's **encrypted key from the CA** (`pki.GetProvisionerKey`, token_generator.go:400) and decrypts it with a password prompt (token_generator.go:406-415). `TokenGenerator.SignSSHToken` (token_generator.go:125-140) embeds `token.WithSSH(provisioner.SignSSHOptions{CertType, KeyID, Principals, ValidAfter, ValidBefore})` and signs with the JWK; default token validity 5 minutes (`token/token.go:20-21`).
7. Client: `flow.GetClient(ctx, token)` (certificate_flow.go:134-171) — if the token payload has `SHA` + http audience, bootstraps with `ca.WithRootSHA256`; otherwise `--ca-url`/`--root` required.
8. **CA call**: `caClient.SSHSign(&api.SSHSignRequest{PublicKey, OTT: token, Principals, CertType, KeyID, ValidAfter, ValidBefore, AddUserPublicKey, IdentityCSR, TemplateData})` (certificate.go:449-463).
9. Identity cert (x509) when `version.RequireClientAuthentication` (certificate.go:368-432): host certs get a **UUID URI SAN** — from `--host-id machine` (blake2b of `/etc/machine-id` with key `"man moon machine"`, converted to v4 UUID, certificate.go:559-581), an explicit UUID, or reused from an existing identity cert (certificate.go:583-607).
10. Output: private key serialized OpenSSH-style, encrypted via prompt or `--password-file` (certificate.go:466-494); pub/cert files 0644 via `marshalPublicKey` (certificate.go:491, 497, 551-557); add-user key triple (certificate.go:502-513); identity cert (certificate.go:516-520).
11. **Agent**: unless `--no-agent`, user certs are added via `sshutil.DialAgent(); agent.AddCertificate(comment, resp.Certificate.Certificate, priv)` (certificate.go:529-540).

### `step ssh login` (`command/ssh/login.go:114-301`)
- **Requires an SSH agent**: `sshutil.DialAgent()` at login.go:156-159 (unix: dials `$SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `internal/sshutil/agent_unix.go:15-25`).
- Idempotency: unless `--force`, fetches CA user roots (`client.SSHRoots()`) and calls `agent.GetKey(comment, WithRemoveExpiredCerts(now), WithSignatureKey(userKeys))` — returns early if a valid CA-signed key with that comment is present (login.go:162-183).
- Token via the same `GenerateSSHToken` flow, with `validAfter` set 1 minute in the past to avoid clock-skew "not yet valid" errors (login.go:190-201).
- OIDC email override of subject (login.go:241-248); identity CSR if required (login.go:250-260); `caClient.SSHSign` (login.go:262-276); `ca.WriteDefaultIdentity` (login.go:279-283); **agent interaction**: `agent.AddCertificate(comment, cert, priv)` (login.go:286-290) and optionally the add-user cert (login.go:291-299).

**Agent internals** (`internal/sshutil/agent.go`): `Agent` wraps `agent.ExtendedAgent` + raw `Conn` (agent.go:84-99); `AddCertificate` computes `LifetimeSecs = ValidBefore - now` (0 = infinity; forced 0 on Windows because the Windows agent rejects lifetimes, agent.go:245-271); `GetKey` matches by comment with filters (agent.go:159-176); `WithSignatureKey` filters keys whose cert signature key matches the CA roots (agent.go:32-52); `WithRemoveExpiredCerts` actively removes expired certs from the agent (agent.go:65-79); `RemoveKeys`/`RemoveAllKeys` for logout (agent.go:201-242). `step ssh list` (list.go:62-106) prints fingerprints or raw keys; `step ssh logout` (logout.go:78-139) removes CA-signed keys only (falls back to `WithCertsOnly()` if roots unavailable, logout.go:112-120).

### `step ssh config` (`command/ssh/config.go:112-304`)
Purpose: installs SSH client/host configuration from CA templates. Applies contexts (`step.Contexts().Apply(ctx)`, config.go:147-150) or bootstraps a team authority (config.go:137-145); wires `loginOnUnauthorized` retry (config.go:153-162). `--roots`/`--federation` print the user/host CA public keys in authorized_keys format (config.go:165-199). Otherwise: builds template data — `GOOS`, `StepPath`, `StepBasePath`, `SSHTemplateVersionKey="v2"`, current `Context`, `Console`, `--set` vars (config.go:201-221); detects `User` from agent certificates signed by the CA (config.go:223-250, error if absent: "please run `step ssh login`"); fetches templates via `client.SSHConfig(req)` (config.go:262-265) and writes them with `t.Write()` or prints with `--dry-run` (config.go:288-301).

### `step ssh proxycommand` (`command/ssh/proxycommand.go:70-96`)
Purpose: an `ssh ProxyCommand` helper. Flow: `doLoginIfNeeded` (proxycommand.go:100-216 — agent `HasKeys(WithSignatureKey, WithRemoveExpiredCerts)`; full login+SSHSign+`AddCertificate` if missing) → `getBastion` via `client.SSHBastion` (proxycommand.go:218-227) → if a bastion is configured, `proxyBastion` re-execs `ssh` (via `exec.Exec`, proxycommand.go:266-295) with bastion user/port/flags and `nc host port` (or a custom command rendered by `sshutil.ProxyCommand`); else `proxyDirect` opens a raw TCP connection and pipes stdin/stdout bidirectionally with half-close semantics (proxycommand.go:229-264; the return-early-on-first-done fix references smallstep/cli#1641 at 246-249). Has a test: `proxycommand_test.go`.

Other subcommands: `check-host` (checkHost.go:61-115 — optional x5c-identity token when client auth required, exit 1 if host unknown), `hosts` (hosts.go — `client.SSHGetHosts` table), `inspect`, `fingerprint`, `needs-renewal`, `rekey`, `renew`, `revoke`.

---

## 5. command/certificate/install.go & uninstall.go — trust stores

Both commands live in one file, `command/certificate/install.go` (definitions 18-156; actions 158-214).

- `getTruststoreOptions` (install.go:216-253): reads the PEM cert (`pemutil.ReadCertificate`), enforces the invariant that it is a **self-signed root CA** — `cert.IsCA && cert.CheckSignatureFrom(cert) == nil` (install.go:222-224); prefix defaults to `Subject.CommonName + " "` or `"Smallstep Development CA "` (install.go:226-233).
- Options mapped to the external library: `truststore.WithPrefix`, `--all` → `WithJava()+WithFirefox()`, individual `--java`/`--firefox`, `--no-system` → `WithNoSystem()` (install.go:235-251).
- Actual install/uninstall is **entirely delegated to `github.com/smallstep/truststore` v0.13.0** (go.mod:24): `truststore.Install(cert, opts...)` / `truststore.Uninstall(...)` (install.go:169, 198). Command failures are unwrapped from `*truststore.CmdError` to show the failed command (install.go:170-174, 199-203).
- Platform coverage (implemented inside the truststore library, not here): OS system trust stores (Linux `update-ca-certificates`-style, macOS keychain via `security`, Windows cert stores), plus optional **Java** keystore and **Firefox** NSS DB.
- After success prints `certinfo.CertificateShortText` (install.go:180-182, 209-211).

---

## 6. command/certificate/create.go — non-CA mode & --kms

Profiles and default validity (`create.go:25-39`): `leaf` 24h, `self-signed` 24h, `intermediate-ca` 10y, `root-ca` 10y, template-based 24h.

**`createAction`** (`create.go:495-771`):
- Args: `<subject> <crt-file> [<key-file>]` (key file omitted when `--key` is given, create.go:496-502). `--no-password` requires `--insecure` (create.go:505-508).
- **Key handling** — `parseOrCreateKey` (create.go:773-836): no `--key` → `keyutil.GenerateKeyPair(kty, crv, size)`, with `keyutil.Insecure()` temporarily enabling sub-2048 RSA under `--insecure` (create.go:786-789). With `--key` → `cryptoutil.CreateSigner(kms, keyFile, opts...)`, falling back to `cryptoutil.PublicKey(kms, keyFile)` when the input is a public key (create.go:820-826); the signer must pass `cryptoutil.IsX509Signer` (create.go:830-832).
- CSR mode `--csr` (create.go:570-640): builds a `x509util` template-driven CSR; incompatible with ca/bundle/profile/time flags (create.go:574-594).
- **Self-signed invariant**: `--profile self-signed` requires `--subtle` (create.go:647-650).
- A public key with `--key` (priv == nil) requires `--skip-csr-signature`; the cert template is then built directly from `certTemplate.PublicKey = pub` instead of from a CSR (create.go:653-656, 695-702).
- **Parent/signer** — `parseSigner` (create.go:841-909): `leaf`/`intermediate-ca` require `--ca` + `--ca-key`; `root-ca`/`self-signed` forbid them and self-sign with `parent = certTemplate` (create.go:716-718). `--ca-kms` selects the KMS for the parent signer (create.go:845, 898).
- Templates per profile: `x509util.DefaultLeafTemplate` / `DefaultIntermediateTemplate` / `DefaultRootTemplate` / `DefaultLeafTemplate` (self-signed) (create.go:669-689); validity applied at create.go:720-733 with an "already expired" guard.
- `x509util.CreateCertificate(certTemplate, parent, pub, signer)` (create.go:735); `--bundle` appends the parent PEM (leaf only, create.go:642-645, 746-752).
- Private key saved unless it is a KMS signer — `!cryptoutil.IsKMSSigner(priv)` (create.go:755-759); `savePrivateKey` (create.go:911-934) uses `--password-file` or prompts; plaintext only via `--no-password`+`--insecure`.

**KMS integration** (`internal/cryptoutil/cryptoutil.go`): the `--kms` flag (documented at `flags/flags.go:471-508`) accepts `yubikey:`, `pkcs11:`, `tpmkms:`, `cloudkms:`, `awskms:`, `azurekms:` URIs. Dispatch logic:
- `IsKMS` (cryptoutil.go:28-38): a **file that exists always wins** over a URI-shaped name; otherwise `kms.TypeOf` must identify a non-default KMS.
- `CreateSigner`/`PublicKey` (cryptoutil.go:52-87): filename → `pemutil.Read`; otherwise a `kmsSigner`/`kmsPublicKey` wrapper (cryptoutil.go:230, 263) that shells out to the external **step-kms-plugin** binary via `plugin.LookPath("kms")` (see `LoadCertificate` exec at cryptoutil.go:99-115; signer `Sign` at 306+, `Attest` at 348).
- `LoadJSONWebKey` (cryptoutil.go:126-169): wraps the KMS signer in `jose.NewOpaqueSigner`, derives `alg` (ES256/384/512, RS256, EdDSA) and a thumbprint `kid` — this is how SSH/JWK tokens can be signed with HSM/KMS keys (`token_generator.go:422`, `generateX5CToken` at token_generator.go:216-233).

---

## 7. command/context — $STEPPATH contexts

`step context` group (`command/context/context.go:10-59`): `current`, `list`, `remove`, `select`. Contexts are named mappings `{authority, profile}` stored in `$STEPPATH/contexts.json`, with the selected one in `$STEPPATH/current-context.json` (documented in `command/path/path.go:39-80`, which also prints `step path [--base|--profile]` resolving to `$STEPPATH/authorities/<name>` and `$STEPPATH/profiles/<name>`).

- **select** (`select.go:34-44`): `step.Contexts().SaveCurrent(name)` — persists the default context.
- **current** (`current.go:46-70`): prints `GetCurrent().Name`, or JSON `{name, authority, profile}` with `--json`; errors "no context selected" if none.
- **list** (`list.go:37-52`): marks the current context with `▶`, then `ListAlphabetical()`.
- **remove** (`remove.go:47-118`): refuses to remove the current context (remove.go:62-64); computes whether the target's `authority`/`profile` directories are shared with other contexts (remove.go:68-82); prompts for confirmation unless `--force` (remove.go:84-100); `os.RemoveAll` of the authority path and profile path when unshared (remove.go:102-111); `cs.Remove(name)` (remove.go:112); finally strips the authority's line from `$STEPPATH/ssh/includes` (remove.go:117).
- The `Contexts()` implementation (enabled/disabled state, storage format) lives in `github.com/smallstep/cli-utils/step` (external). This repo's touchpoints: `step.Contexts().Apply(ctx)` honors `--context` flags (e.g. `command/ssh/config.go:147-150`); `Enabled()`/`GetCurrent()` used in ssh config (config.go:207-209).
- **defaults.json**: written by `step ca bootstrap` at `$STEPPATH/config/defaults.json` (`utils/cautils/bootstrap.go:146`, 169-195 — CA URL, root fingerprint/path, redirect URL, provisioner, min password length; profile-scoped defaults file when contexts are enabled, bootstrap.go:197-209). Context creation during bootstrap: `AddContext` + `SaveCurrent` + `SetCurrent` (bootstrap.go:130-141). `flags.Identity` exists specifically so identity can be configured in defaults.json (`flags/flags.go:451-457`); CA commands read defaults.json (`command/ca/token.go:55`, `command/ca/health.go:39-42`).

---

## 8. autocomplete directory & command/completion

- `step completion <shell>` (`command/completion/completion.go:15-123`): supports **bash**, **zsh**, **fish**. Bash and zsh scripts are embedded string literals (completion.go:56-98); both work by invoking the CLI itself with urfave/cli's `--generate-bash-completion` (with the zsh `_CLI_ZSH_AUTOCOMPLETE_HACK=1` env trick and flag completion when the current word starts with `-`). Fish uses `ctx.App.ToFishCompletion()` (completion.go:112-117). `BashComplete` on the command suggests `bash/zsh/fish` (completion.go:43-50).
- Shell completion generation is enabled app-wide: `app.EnableBashCompletion = true` (`internal/cmd/root.go:124`).
- `autocomplete/` directory: **deprecated** (`autocomplete/README.md:1-2`) — `bash_autocomplete` and `zsh_autocomplete` are the same scripts shipped as files for packaging; users are directed to `step completion <shell>` instead.

---

## Cross-cutting invariants worth noting

1. **Misuse gating**: `--subtle`/`--insecure` are mandatory for risky operations (crypto.go:32-37; self-signed certs create.go:647-650; `no-password` needs `--insecure`; jwt `inspect` needs `--insecure`; `no-exp-check` needs `--insecure`).
2. **JWK `use` enforcement**: `sig` keys rejected for encryption, `enc` keys rejected for signing (jwt sign.go:331-333; jwe encrypt.go:247-249; jwe decrypt.go:143-145).
3. **Key material protection**: private keys/JWKs written 0600; private JWKs stored JWE-encrypted (PBES2-HS256+A128KW @600k iterations, `jwk+json` content type); JWK Set files are flock-protected.
4. **kid semantics**: thumbprint-derived kids by default; `--jwks` requires a kid (flag or token header) and selection happens inside `go.step.sm/crypto/jose`.
5. **OAuth security**: PKCE S256 + state + nonce on the loopback flow; 2-minute callback timeout; the loopback server is a random-port `httptest.Server` unless `--listen`; refresh tokens are surfaced but never used.
6. **SSH tokens**: audience is `<ca-url>/1.0/ssh/sign`, 5-minute default validity, `validAfter` back-dated 1 minute in login/proxycommand to tolerate clock skew; agent certificate lifetime mirrors `ValidBefore` (0 on Windows).
7. **CA client authentication**: when `version.RequireClientAuthentication` is true, every SSH flow provisions an x509 identity cert (`ca.CreateIdentityRequest` + `ca.WriteDefaultIdentity`) and hosts get a UUID URI SAN derived from `/etc/machine-id` (blake2b) or an existing identity cert.
</task_result>
</task>

All research complete. Here is the report.

# Findings: local certificate utility commands in smallstep `step`

All subcommands of `step certificate` are registered at `command/certificate/certificate.go:84-98` (bundle, create, format, inspect, fingerprint, lint, needs-renewal, sign, verify, key, install, uninstall, p12).

## 1. `command/certificate/bundle.go`
- Simple concatenation: exactly 3 positional args `<crt-file> <ca> <bundle-file>` (bundle.go:55). Reads each file, PEM-decodes only the *first* block (bundle.go:64, 74), writes leaf PEM followed by CA PEM to the bundle with mode 0600 (bundle.go:80-83).
- Order is **leaf-first, issuer second** — no chain building, no validation of the relationship, no `$STEP`/dir interpolation (plain `os.ReadFile`). Only flag: `--force` (bundle.go:50).

## 2. `command/certificate/inspect.go`
- Local file or remote URL (STDIN with `-`, inspect.go:200-202). Remote detection via `trimURL` and TLS dial in `command/certificate/remote.go:35-95`; port prefixes: tcp/tls/https 443, smtps 465, ldaps 636 (remote.go:15-21).
- `--format text|json|pem`, default text (inspect.go:130-146, 204-206). `--short` only valid with text (207-209). Text output uses `certinfo.CertificateText/ShortText` (253-267); JSON uses **zcrypto** `zx509.ParseCertificate` then JSON-encodes (268-293); PEM re-encodes raw certs (294-301).
- Default prints only the **first** certificate; `--bundle` prints all in file order (219-222, 241-244). CSR detection fallback when no CERTIFICATE blocks (229-237). Remote flags: `--roots` (file, comma-separated list, or directory — via `x509util.ReadCertPool`), `--servername`, `--insecure` (inspect.go:147-179; remote.go:40-58).

## 3. `command/certificate/fingerprint.go`
- Default hash **SHA-256** (fingerprint.go:169); `--sha1` exists but requires `--insecure` (126-128, 170-172).
- `--format` default `hex`; accepted values hex, base64, base64-url, base64-raw, base64-url-raw, emoji via `flags.ParseFingerprintFormat` (flags/flags.go:546-564). Uses `go.step.sm/crypto/fingerprint.New` over `crt.Raw` (173-183).
- Also works on CSRs (raw bytes hashed, 152-159) and remote URLs; `--bundle` prints `i: fp` indexed lines (178-179), otherwise only first cert (165-167).

## 4. `command/certificate/lint.go`
- Uses `github.com/smallstep/zlint` + `github.com/smallstep/zcrypto/x509`: parses the cert into a zcrypto certificate and calls `zlint.LintCertificate`, then prints the `zlint.ResultSet` as indented JSON (lint.go:130-141).
- Input: local PEM file (first block only) or remote URL (114-127). Flags: `--roots`, `--insecure`, `--servername` (67-90). **No `--priority`/`-p` flag exists in this version** (repo-wide grep found none).

## 5. `command/certificate/verify.go`
- Pure local RFC 5280 path validation with `crypto/x509`: first PEM block = leaf, all remaining CERTIFICATE blocks become the intermediates pool (verify.go:195-220); `cert.Verify` with `KeyUsages: ExtKeyUsageAny` (231-244). There is no `--bundle` flag, but a bundled input file works because extras feed the intermediate pool; `--roots` loads a root pool from file/list/dir (223-229); `--host` sets DNSName check.
- Optional revocation checks: `--verify-ocsp` (+`--ocsp-endpoint`) using `golang.org/x/crypto/ocsp` POST requests (341-372, 380-414); `--verify-crl` (+`--crl-endpoint`) downloads the CRL, checks issuer signature (skipped with `--insecure`) and serial revocation via `crlutil.ParseCRL` (308-339, 416-455). Issuer comes from `--issuing-ca` or the cert's IssuingCertificateURL AIA (269-306). Exit 0 on success, non-zero on failure (242-243, 336-338, 369-371).

## 6. `needs-renewal` — exit code semantics (systemd-timer relevant)
- `command/certificate/needsRenewal.go`: exit **0** = needs renewal, **1** = does not need renewal (silent with `cli.NewExitError("", 1)` unless `--verbose`), **2** = cert file does not exist, **255** = any other error (needsRenewal.go:44-48, 146, 172, 230-243).
- Default threshold: renewal needed once ≥ **66%** of the lifetime has elapsed (`defaultPercentUsedThreshold`, line 20; percent math 211-217). `--expires-in` accepts a percent (`75%`) or Go duration (`1h15m`); percent validated 0-100 (184-206). `--bundle` checks every cert in chain, default leaf only (208-225, 131-134). Remote hostnames supported via the same trimURL/getPeerCertificates path.
- **There is no `step ca needs-renewal`** — only `step certificate needs-renewal` and `step ssh needs-renewal` (command/ssh/needsRenewal.go:22, registered at command/ssh/ssh.go:94).

## 7. `command/certificate/p12.go`
- Uses `software.sslmate.com/src/go-pkcs12` (p12.go:9). Encoder is `pkcs12.Modern` by default, `--legacy` switches to `pkcs12.LegacyRC2` (PBE+SHA1+RC2 certs / 3DES keys) (104-107).
- With `<crt> <key>` args: builds an identity store; first cert of the input bundle is the leaf, remaining certs are appended to the `--ca` intermediates (156-176). With only `--ca` (repeatable): builds a Java/Windows trust store with FriendlyName `"<subject> - <fingerprint>"` (177-190).
- Password from `--password-file` or interactive prompt; `--no-password` requires `--insecure` (120-125, 138-153). Output written 0600 (192).

## 8. `format.go` and `key.go`
- **format**: converts PEM↔ASN.1 DER for a certificate or CSR. PEM detected by `-----BEGIN ` substring; DER branch tries x509 cert then CSR parse (format.go:90-110). Writes to stdout or `--out`, preserving the input file's mode when writing to disk (112-125).
- **key**: extracts the embedded public key from a cert/CSR (first PEM block only, `pemutil.ParseKey(..., WithFirstBlock())`) — or prints a private key if the file contains only one — serializes back to PEM; `--out` to save 0600 (key.go:73-92).

## 9. `command/crl/` + `internal/crlutil`
- `step crl` currently has a single subcommand `inspect` (command/crl/crl.go:24-26). `step crl inspect <file|url>`: reads CRL from file, STDIN (`-`), or HTTP(S) URL; `--from <cert-url|file>` fetches the cert and uses its first CRLDistributionPoint, with the rest of the chain as CA certs (inspect.go:161-196).
- Refuses to run without `--insecure` unless `--ca` (or derivable CA via `--from`) is given (120-122). Formats: `--format text` (default, `crlutil.PrintCRL`), `json`, `pem` (240-254). Signature validity checked against `--ca` certs by matching SKI/AKI (227-238).
- `internal/crlutil`: JSON CRL model (crlutil.go:22-33), `ParseCRL` accepts PEM or DER (42-48), `CRL.Verify` checks nextUpdate, CA expiry and signature (93-110), `VerifySignature` supports ECDSA, RSA PKCS1v15 + RSA-PSS, Ed25519 (112-139), `PrintCRL` human-readable text (141+).

## 10. `command/fileserver/`
- **Hidden** command (`Hidden: true`, fileserver.go:30), self-described as "experimental and only intended for test purposes" (40). Serves a directory via `http.FileServer(http.Dir(root))` (154) over HTTP or HTTPS (`--cert`/`--key`, min TLS 1.2), `--address` defaults `:0` (random port), `--pidfile` support (139-146).
- `--roots` enables mTLS with `RequireAndVerifyClientCert` (241-249); SIGHUP reloads cert/key/client-CA files live via `tlsRenewer` (187-208, 233-267). Relation to ACME: the `step ca certificate --webroot` docs reference "an existing fileserver" for challenge files (command/ca/ca.go:134-140); standalone mode runs its own challenge server inside the step process rather than this command.

## 11. `command/base64/`
- RFC 4648 encode/decode of args (space-joined) or stdin (base64.go:85-103). Flags: `-d/--decode`, `-r/--raw` (unpadded), `-u/--url` (URL-safe alphabet) (66-79, 119-141).
- On decode, encoding is auto-detected when neither `-r` nor `-u` is set: raw if no `=` padding suffix, URL if it contains `-`/`_` (125-128).

## 12. `command/beta/`
- `step beta` = "commands that are being tested; these APIs are likely to change" (beta.go:15). Contains only `ca.BetaCommand()` (beta.go:19-21; command/ca/ca.go:158-169), which contains only `acme.Command()` (ca.go:166-168) → `eab.Command()` (command/ca/acme/acme.go:16-18).
- Net effect: `step beta ca acme eab list|add|remove` — manage ACME External Account Binding Keys through the CA Admin API (`client.CreateExternalAccountKey` etc.) (command/ca/acme/eab/eab.go:44-76; add.go:73-94). Rationale: "beta access to new step-ca APIs. These commands may change, disappear, or be promoted" (ca.go:164-165). If the CA returns not-implemented, it's mapped to a "only available in Certificate Manager" upsell message (eab.go:81-89).

## 13. `internal/kdf` and `pkg/bcrypt_pbkdf`
- `internal/kdf`: password-hashing library behind `step crypto kdf hash|compare` (command/crypto/kdf/kdf.go:19-20). Provides `Scrypt` (scrypt-32768 default), `Bcrypt` (MCF string), `Argon2i`, `Argon2id` — all emit PHC-format strings with random 16-byte salt (kdf.go:24-83, phc.go); `Compare`/`CompareString` re-derive and constant-time compare (kdf.go:85-137).
- `pkg/bcrypt_pbkdf`: vendored Go implementation of OpenBSD `bcrypt_pbkdf(3)` (bcrypt-based PBKDF2 variant), API `Key(password, salt, rounds, keyLen)` (pkg/bcrypt_pbkdf/bcrypt_pbkdf.go:5-7, README). No internal importers found — kept for compatibility with external importers (nolint comment at line 5).

## 14. Misc helpers
- `utils/cli.go`: `GetKeyDetailsFromCLI` normalizes `--kty/--curve/--size`: RSA default 2048 (rejects <2048 unless insecure), EC default P-256 (P-256/384/521), OKP default Ed25519; no kty flag → EC P-256 (cli.go:12-84).
- `utils/read.go`: `FileExists`, `ReadAll`, `ReadString`, `ReadPasswordFromFile` (right-trims whitespace), `ReadStringPasswordFromFile`, `ReadInput` (prompts if stdin isn't piped), `ReadFile` — supports `-` = STDIN and strips UTF BOM via `utils/internal/utfbom` (read.go:21-107). These back the ubiquitous STDIN `-` behavior.
- `utils/sysutils`: thin, build-tag-split wrappers over syscalls: `Flock`, `FileLock` (LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB), `FileUnlock`, `Kill`, `Exec` (sysutils.go:5-22; sysutils_unix.go:9-27). Callers: `exec/exec.go:47` (step exec/daemon), `command/crypto/jwk/keyset.go:240-297` (JWK set file locking), `command/ca/renew.go:395` (signalling the CA to reload).
- `utils/utils.go`: `Fail` (prints stack traces when `STEPDEBUG=1`, exits 1) and `CompleteURL` (normalizes incomplete CA URLs, defaults https scheme).

# How to add a new Command

Before making any changes, please consult the [CLI style guide](https://github.com/urfave/cli)!

### Package Layout

The [`urfave/cli`](https://github.com/urfave/cli) package that forms the basis
of Step CLI supports N-levels of command hierarchy. Each level of the hierarchy
should exist within its own package if possible. For example, `version` and
`help` exist inside their own packages inside the top-level `command` package.

Any package used by a command but does not contain explicit business logic
directly related to the command should exist in the top-level of this
repository. For example, the `github.com/smallstep/cli/flags` and
`github.com/smallstep/cli-utils/errs` package are used by many different commands and
contain functionality for defining flags and creating/manipulating errors.

### Adding a Command

Once you figured out where to add the command inside the package hierarchy you
must register the command. This way the command *can* be made available if
desired inside the `cmd/step/main.go`.

An example of defining a command and registering it:

```golang
package validate

import (
  "github.com/urfave/cli"

  "github.com/smallstep/cli/command"
  "github.com/smallstep/cli/flags"
)

func init() {
  cmd := cli.Command{
    Name: "validate",
    Usage: "Returns whether or not the provided token is valid",
    Flags: []cli.Flag{
      flags.Token("The one-time token value to validate"),
    },
    Action: validate,
  }

  command.Register(validate)
}
```

Once this is done, you then must import the pkg inside `cmd/step/main.go` so
the packages `init` method is run appropriately. This only needs to be done for
top-level commands.

```golang
package main

import (
  "github.com/urfave/cli"

  _ "github.com/smallstep/cli/validate"
)
```

This will ensure that the `smallstep/cli/validate` package is initialized
and thus registered with the `smallstep/cli/command`.

### Usage, Flags, Errors, and Prompts

There are three packages which contain functionality to make writing commands easier:

- `github.com/smallstep/cli/flags`
- `github.com/smallstep/cli/prompts`
- `github.com/smallstep/cli-utils/errs`
- `github.com/smallstep/cli-utils/usage`

The usage package is used to extend the default documentation provided by
`urfave/cli` by enabling us to document arguments, whether they are optional or
required, and ensuring they're printed out as a part of the `step help` or
`step <command> -h` flow. If you need to add a different type of annotation to
document an argument just add it to the `usage.Argument` struct!

When you add a flag, look into the preexisting ones inside the `flags`
package. Could you use one of the preexisting flags in order to reduce
duplication? If not, make sure to add a flag so it could be used in future!

The `errs` package contains functionality for defining and working with errors
to ensure they are mutated properly into a `urfave/cli.ExitError` which ensures
the process returns an appropriate exit code on termination. When you create an
error, consider whether or not it's general and could be predefined inside the
`errs` package. Errors that are specific to the command itself should exist
only inside that commands respective package.

The `prompts` package is a small wrapper around the various different types of
prompts used by the commands. If you need a new prompt, consider adding a new
function to this package to tailor the prompt for the step cli. This way other
commands can adopt the step aesthetic as new functionality is introduced.

### Hiding a Command

Sometimes it's desirable to prevent a command from showing up in the help menu
because it's been deprecated *or* it's not ready for users to leverage. This
can be achieved by setting the `Hidden` property on the `cli.Command` struct to
`true`.

package certificate

import (
	"github.com/urfave/cli"

	"github.com/smallstep/cli-utils/command"
)

// Command returns the cli.Command for jwt and related subcommands.
func init() {
	cmd := cli.Command{
		Name:      "certificate",
		Usage:     "create, revoke, validate, bundle, and otherwise manage certificates",
		UsageText: "step certificate SUBCOMMAND [ARGUMENTS] [GLOBAL_FLAGS] [SUBCOMMAND_FLAGS]",
		Description: `**step certificate** command group provides facilities for creating
certificate signing requests (CSRs), creating self-signed certificates
(e.g., for use as a root certificate authority), generating leaf or
intermediate CA certificate by signing a CSR, validating certificates,
renewing certificates, generating certificate bundles, and key-wrapping
of private keys.

## EXAMPLES

Create a root certificate and private key using the default parameters (EC P-256 curve):
'''
$ step certificate create foo foo.crt foo.key --profile root-ca
'''

Create a leaf certificate and private key using the default parameters (EC P-256 curve):
'''
$ step certificate create baz baz.crt baz.key --ca ./foo.crt --ca-key ./foo.key
'''

Create a CSR and private key using the default parameters (EC P-256 curve):
'''
$ step certificate create zap zap.csr zap.key --csr
'''

Sign a CSR and generate a signed certificate:
'''
$ step certificate sign zap.csr foo.crt foo.key
'''

Inspect the contents of a certificate:
'''
$ step certificate inspect ./baz.crt
'''

Verify the signature of a certificate:
'''
$ step certificate verify ./baz.crt --roots ./foo.crt
'''

Lint the contents of a certificate to check for common errors and missing fields:
'''
$ step certificate lint ./baz.crt
'''

Bundle an end certificate with the issuing certificate:
'''

31: 		return false
32: 	}
33: 	_, err := os.Stat(path)
34: 	return err == nil
35: }
36: 
37: // ReadAll returns a slice of bytes with the content of the given reader.
38: func ReadAll(r io.Reader) ([]byte, error) {
39: 	b, err := io.ReadAll(r)
40: 	return b, errors.Wrap(err, "error reading data")
41: }
42: 
43: // ReadString reads one line from the given io.Reader.
44: func ReadString(r io.Reader) (string, error) {
45: 	br := bufio.NewReader(r)
46: 	str, err := br.ReadString('\n')
47: 	if err != nil && err != io.EOF {
48: 		return "", errors.Wrap(err, "error reading string")
49: 	}
50: 	return strings.TrimSpace(str), nil
51: }
52: 
53: // ReadPasswordFromFile reads and returns the password from the given filename.
54: // The contents of the file will be trimmed at the right.
55: func ReadPasswordFromFile(filename string) ([]byte, error) {
56: 	password, err := os.ReadFile(filename) // #nosec G703 -- file intended to be provided by user
57: 	if err != nil {
58: 		return nil, errs.FileError(err, filename)
59: 	}
60: 	password = bytes.TrimRightFunc(password, unicode.IsSpace)
61: 	return password, nil
62: }
63: 
64: // ReadStringPasswordFromFile reads and returns the password from the given filename.
65: // The contents of the file will be trimmed at the right.
66: func ReadStringPasswordFromFile(filename string) (string, error) {
67: 	b, err := ReadPasswordFromFile(filename)
68: 	if err != nil {
69: 		return "", err
70: 	}
71: 	return string(b), nil
72: }
73: 
74: // ReadInput from stdin if something is detected or ask the user for an input
75: // using the given prompt.
76: func ReadInput(prompt string) ([]byte, error) {
77: 	st, err := stdin.Stat()
78: 	if err != nil {
79: 		return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "error reading data")
80: 	}
81: 
82: 	if st.Size() == 0 && st.Mode()&os.ModeNamedPipe == 0 {
83: 		return ui.PromptPassword(prompt)
84: 	}
85: 
86: 	return ReadAll(stdin)
87: }
88: 
89: // ReadFile returns the contents of the file identified by name. It reads from
90: // STDIN if name is a hyphen ("-").
91: func ReadFile(name string) (b []byte, err error) {
92: 	if name == stdinFilename {
93: 		name = "/dev/stdin"
94: 		b, err = io.ReadAll(stdin)
95: 	} else {
96: 		var contents []byte
97: 		contents, err = os.ReadFile(name) // #nosec G703 -- file intended to be provided by user
98: 		if err != nil {
99: 			return nil, errs.FileError(err, name)
100: 		}
101: 		b, err = io.ReadAll(utfbom.SkipOnly(bytes.NewReader(contents)))
102: 	}
103: 	if err != nil {
104: 		return nil, errs.FileError(err, name)
105: 	}
106: 	return b, nil
107: }
